title: Red Dye in White Wine Got Tasters to Describe Red Wine Aromas
hook: White wine with an odorless red dye fooled the noses of 54 students
summary: White wine dyed red with an odorless dye was described in red wine aroma words by 54 oenology undergraduates.

text: The participants were 54 undergraduate students in the enology program at the University of Bordeaux.
In the first week, they tasted red and white wine and chose words from a list of aroma terms.
A week later, they were given two glasses again, holding the same list.
One glass was white wine. The other was that same white wine with red dye added.

panels.text: Just adding dye changes how they rate the smell?

text: Yet the students who got the red-looking white mostly reused the words they had used for red wine.
The red words were things like blackcurrant, raspberry, cherry and prune.

panels.text: So the nose smelled it, but the eyes butted in.

text: Their interpretation is that the tasters ignored smell because of what they saw.
This paper alone can't tell us that professional tasters would do the same.
